correctness.rationale: For every n>=2 and integer p,q>=1, disconnected coalitions have -infinity welfare, hence optimal coalitions are interval blocks. Each size l has welfare w_l=2p(l-1)-q(l-1)(l-2); strict concavity yields exact equalized lengths for each number of blocks, giving the displayed max and binomial count. Endpoint optimality makes all current individual utilities nonnegative; every feasible profitable boundary transfer would increase welfare by twice its gain, hence all maxima are Nash. The density difference 2(p+q)/(l(l+1))-q has at most one zero, producing only adjacent critical sizes. An off-critical density deficit uniformly bounds exceptional block vertices; at criticality coprime block sizes yield exact recurrence and a unique simple dominant pole. Direct verifier run independently checks small complete set partitions and Nash moves, not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The precise count of ALL optimal coalition configurations, combined with every-optimum Nash stability, gives an interpretable structural benchmark for a natural connected friend/enemy coalition model on paths. At explicit critical penalty ratios the number of welfare-optimal outcomes shifts from a polynomial upper bound to exponential growth; this distinguishes generic robust choices from degenerate high-multiplicity optimum landscapes. This infinite-family phase diagram is not merely a finite search exercise, a known-table recomputation or a generic application of an algorithm.
